title: SYSK Selects: How Gold Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2013 episode "How Gold Works." Josh and Chuck cover gold's history from ancient Egypt, Nubia, and Lydia's first minted coins through Greek and Roman coinage, Inca gold leaf, Marco Polo and Columbus, El Dorado and Brazil's gold region, and the North Carolina, California, Australian and South African gold rushes. They explain modern gold prospecting, open pit and underground mining, placer panning, cyanide heap extraction, electrowinning, smelting and refining into 99.9 percent ingots, karats and alloys, gold's industrial uses in electronics, NASA and dental crowns, the environmental costs of mining and illegal mercury mining in Guiana, the gold standard, and Fort Knox. The episode closes with a listener mail from a communications professor.

segments.title: Opening banter and gold's ancient history
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the show's name and a Mayan and Aztec intro, then cover Aztec and Egyptian reverence for gold, Nubia, gold's chemical symbol Au, and gold's rarity: about 161,000 tons ever mined, with roughly 15 percent unaccounted for.

segments.title: Early coinage and gold in the Americas and Europe
segments.summary: The hosts discuss early smithing of gold, Croesus of Lydia minting the first gold coins, Greek and Roman coinage, Inca gold leaf work, medieval European gold coins, Marco Polo, Columbus, and Ferdinand's order to get gold.

segments.title: El Dorado, gold rushes in North Carolina, California and Australia
segments.summary: Discussion of the El Dorado legend and Minas Gerais in Brazil, the North Carolina gold rush as the first US gold rush, the California gold rush and Delonega panning, and the Australian gold rush of the 1850s.

segments.title: South Africa and modern gold production
segments.summary: Mention of George Harrison's South African gold discovery in 1868, South Africa as the leading gold producer, and Nevada as the top US producer.

segments.title: Prospecting and mining methods
segments.summary: Explanation of prospecting, the use of equipment to find concentrated gold, and open pit and underground mining methods for lode deposits, plus panning for placer deposits in streams.

segments.title: Gold extraction, cyanide leaching, electrowinning and refining
segments.summary: Ore is crushed and ground, mixed into a slurry with cyanide and oxygen, the gold is adsorbed onto carbon and stripped, electrowinning deposits gold on a negative terminal, and the resulting dore bars are refined to about 99.9 percent pure ingots using soda ash and borax.

segments.title: Karats, alloys, and gold uses in jewelry, electronics and dentistry
segments.summary: Discussion of white, red, and rose gold alloys, karat percentages by country, jewelry making up about two-thirds of gold use, gold's conductivity and corrosion resistance in electronics, NASA's use of gold on the Space Shuttle Columbia, and gold dental crowns.

segments.title: Environmental impact of gold mining and illegal mining
segments.summary: Mining produces large amounts of waste per ounce, cyanide effluent dumped into the ocean, the Earthworks No Dirty Gold campaign, and illegal mercury-based gold mining in Guiana citing a Harper's article by Damon Tabor.

segments.title: Gold standard, Fort Knox and asteroid gold
segments.summary: Brief discussion of the gold standard from 1900 to 1971, Fort Knox gold holdings and their value, and speculation about gold in asteroids.

segments.title: Listener mail from Professor Tom
segments.summary: A communications professor praises the show's life lessons for students and the hosts reflect on his email. The episode closes with a sign-off directing listeners to the website and social channels.
